title: NpcBodyWriteSite - entity appearance/type fields [e+0x88..0x8B] are written by 0x405630 (mov dword [esi+0x88], ebp) from 10 server-packet call sites; [e+0x8A] is the body byte read for special-appearance dispatch
objective: Close player-composition-evidence.json pending item 'gender->type byte [e+0x88] write site (no static writer; entity build path / server packet, candidate)' by locating the static writer of the entity appearance fields at offset 0x88-0x8B, including the body byte 0x8A.
question: Where is the entity appearance/body byte [e+0x8A] (and its neighbors 0x88/0x89/0x8B) written, and how does the value flow from server packets?
method: Full byte-level scan of Mir3.exe for every write instruction touching offsets 0x85-0x8F (ModRM-complete, both disp8 and disp32 forms, byte/word/dword, immediate and register sources), eliminating false positives from non-mem operands (0x8B opcode bytes in arithmetic), then tracing the remaining real write sites and their callers to the server packet handlers.
no_direct_byte_write: There is NO direct single-byte write to [reg+0x8A] anywhere in the binary (byte-scan of C6/88 disp8 and disp32 forms = 0 hits; word 66 89/66 C7 = 0 hits; dword 89 = 0 hits). The field is written only as part of the 4-byte store [esi+0x88] at 0x405862.

write_site.function: 0x405630 (entity appearance/type update; first arg ebp = appearance value, this = esi)
write_site.instruction: 0x405862: mov dword ptr [esi+0x88], ebp - writes [e+0x88]=type byte, [e+0x89], [e+0x8A]=body low byte, [e+0x8B]=body high byte in one 4-byte store
write_site.prologue: 0x405630: ebp=[esp+8] (arg), esi=ecx (this); calls 0x4055B0 validator; dispatches on ebp&0xFF via jump table 0x405894 (case index table 0x4058A8, <0x32)

case_writes.0x405862: [e+0x88] = ebp (unconditional, main line - the appearance/type+body store)

write_site.coord_writes: [e+0xB4]/[e+0xB8]/[e+0xBC] from lookup tables 0x8AA5C0/0x8AA5C8/0x8AA686 (map coordinate offsets), [e+0xC0..0xC2]/[e+0xC4] from args

callers: 0x004052F7 (inside server entity dispatcher 0x404FB0: after writing [e+0x8C]/[e+0xB4..0xE8] and action field [e+0x629C8]; 0x405630 called with the appearance arg then coordinates)
0x0040C390 (inside 0x40C3B0: entity appearance packet handler - packet struct at [esp+4]: word[+6]->[e+0xCC], word[+8]->[e+0xD0], byte[+0xA] stored; then 0x405630(arg=[esp+0xC]))
0x0040F429 (inside 0x40F420: server appearance/action packet handler - calls 0x405630 then writes action [e+0x629C8] from arg[+0x10]/[+0x14])
body_read_dispatch: 0x40C3D0: mov al,[esi+0x8A]; cmp al,0x1C; jne -> else path (special appearance 0x1C=28 triggers 0x401670 equip/swap path with 3 args; else uses generic path)
verdict: CLOSED - [e+0x88..0x8B] appearance/type+body fields have exactly one static write site 0x405862 (mov dword [esi+0x88], ebp inside 0x405630), fed by 10 server-packet call sites; the 42 byte-reads of [..+0x8A] are consumers (animation/action selection), not writers
conclusions: The entity appearance block [e+0x88..0x8B] (type byte 0x88, unknown 0x89, body 16-bit 0x8A/0x8B) is written as one 4-byte store at 0x405862 inside 0x405630 - resolving the pending item's 'no static writer' claim.

0x405630's first argument (ebp = [esp+8]) is the appearance/body value from the server packet; the function validates it (0x4055B0, <0x32 dispatcher) and writes kind byte [e+0x8C] per case plus the unconditional 4-byte store to [e+0x88].
All 10 call sites are server-packet handlers (0x404FB0 entity dispatcher and per-packet handlers like 0x40C3B0/0x40F420), confirming the value origin is server-side appearance codes.

[e+0x8A] is consumed at 0x40C3D0 (cmp 0x1C = special appearance 28, drives 0x401670 equip/swap) and at 0x405A0F/0x405A1D (bx = [e+0x8B]<<8 | [e+0x8A] looked up in table 0x8AA5A8 for animation selection) - all reads, no writes.
The 2 single-byte writes to [e+0x8B]=0 (0x40C773/0x40F456) are clamps (if >= 0x1E), not primary writers.
42 read sites of [..+0x8A] span animation selection (0x405A0F family), appearance dispatch (0x40C3D0), and render paths - all downstream consumers of the 0x405862 store.
